name: Acute Upper Respiratory Tract Infection
description: An acute infection of the upper respiratory tract, most often viral. The common cold is a frequent form and typically causes nasal congestion or rhinorrhea, cough, sneezing and sore throat, usually resolving without antibiotics.
risk_factors: Close contact with a person with a respiratory viral infection
Reduced immunity or chronic illness may increase complication risk
physical_examination: Assessment of temperature and respiratory status
Evaluation for focal lower respiratory findings when symptoms suggest complications
recommended_investigations: Influenza or SARS-CoV-2 testing when results may alter management, particularly in higher-risk patients
Further testing when symptoms are prolonged, severe or suggest another diagnosis
red_flags: Symptoms that improve then significantly worsen
Worsening of a chronic cardiopulmonary condition
contraindications: Routine antibiotics are not appropriate for an uncomplicated viral common cold or nonspecific viral URTI.
